title: Cross-environment memory degradation and KV state drift — customer escalations and runtime patch
creator: Luca Morales
description: Multiple customers (hosted, dedicated, and private deployments) reported a recent uptick in inference request failures and degraded throughput. Root-of-symptoms: increasing native memory use over long-lived sessions leading to GPU OOMs, combined with gradual divergence (drift) and corruption in the in-memory KV prefix cache that made cache lookups return stale or malformed entries. Secondary symptom: heap fragmentation on certain allocator paths that made peak working set exceed physical memory even when aggregate allocation appeared within limits. This ticket centralizes triage, mitigations, and a short-term runtime patch for the next minor release.
timeline_summary: 2026-02-12: First customer report (hosted) of intermittent OOMs on large-context chat workloads.
2026-02-15: Similar errors reported from a Dedicated customer during high-concurrency replay tests.
2026-02-17: Private deployment customer files escalation with crash dumps showing corrupted KV entries and sustained native heap growth.
2026-02-18: P0 declared and cross-team incident channel opened.
2026-02-25: Initial mitigations (node reboots, reduced concurrency) provided partial relief; replication of corruption in internal sim cluster.
2026-03-03: Repro harness shows allocator slab fragmentation under repeated short-lived micro-alloc patterns and a rare KV eviction race.
2026-03-10: Patch candidate (allocator coalescing + KV eviction serialization) validated in canary; degraded latency within SLOs.
2026-03-11: Preparing rollout plan for runtime-1.19.1 and backport to 1.18 LTS.
2026-03-20: targeted release date for runtime-1.19.1 (soft target)
reproduction_steps: 1) Start long-lived session with a sequence of 250+ prefix-heavy requests using token lengths > 8k.
2) Use workload that alternates many short generation requests (burst traffic) and occasional long completions to exercise allocator patterns.
3) Enable KV prefix caching and disable aggressive TTLs to force cache churn.
4) Observe native memory growth and intermittent malformed entries returned from cache lookups after ~1000 iterations.
5) Attach jemalloc/sanitizer to confirm fragmentation growth and run heap profile sampler for top allocation paths.
mitigations_applied: - Temporarily capped concurrency and model token limits for affected customers.
- Forced periodic KV compaction job (every 10m) to reduce drift window.
- Rolled emergency config disabling background batch coalescing on select Dedicated pools.
- Provided step-by-step remediation playbook to Private customers (node restart + cache wipe).
investigation_notes: Heap profiler points to many short-lived arena allocations in the runtime allocator path used by KV cache entries and request-context buffers.
Race condition in eviction path: concurrent compaction + insert could leave tombstoned entries that later read paths interpret as valid leading to malformed output.
Under specific alignment patterns the allocator fails to coalesce freed spans leading to fragmentation and large contiguous allocation failures on GPU pinned buffers.
No evidence of hardware GPU driver corruption; reproduces on multiple kernel versions and both hosted cloud and on-prem hardware.
patch_plan: 1) Fix eviction race: add lightweight eviction mutex per shard and stronger tombstone lifecycle guarantees.
2) Adjust allocator: enable slab coalescing for medium-sized spans and introduce periodic background defragmenter for long-lived nodes.
3) Add defensive validation: CRC checks on KV entries when reading from cache to detect corruption and fall back to recompute rather than return malformed payloads.
4) Add metrics and traces: per-shard eviction latency, tombstone counts, fragmentation ratio, and KV validation failures.
5) Canary rollout strategy: progressive deploy across hosted -> dedicated pools -> private via customer opt-in; automated rollback on error rate increase.
status_updates: 2026-02-18: Incident declared and cross-functional team assigned (runtime, infra, QA).
2026-02-20: Repro harness created and initial reproducer validated in synthetic cluster.
2026-02-28: Root-cause narrowed to eviction race + allocator fragmentation; proposal drafted.
2026-03-03: Patch candidate 1 built (eviction lock + CRC validation); functional tests green.
2026-03-06: Allocator coalescing added to patch; memory regressions verified fixed in stress run.
2026-03-09: Canary rollout initiated on two low-traffic hosted regions; no regressions observed after 48h.
2026-03-11: Approved for broader canary; release engineering prepping runtime-1.19.1 build and docs.
resolution_notes: Planned release: runtime-1.19.1 containing eviction serialization, allocator coalescing, KV CRC validation, and new observability.
Backport plan: cherry-pick critical fixes to runtime-1.18-stable branch for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers who cannot upgrade immediately.
Post-release: run 30-day canary monitoring with retention of memory/fragmentation metrics and weekly check-ins with impacted customers.
Long-term: evaluate replacing in-memory KV cache with a hybrid memory+disk LRU for very long-lived sessions to bound resident set.
qa_and_rollout: - QA: run 72h stress with mixed short/long requests, validate no CRC failures and fragmentation stays bounded.
- Canary: 3 phases (5%, 25%, 100% in non-critical regions) with automated rollback thresholds on error rate and tail latency.
- Private: provide patch bundle and upgrade playbook; offer support window for onsite upgrades and post-upgrade validation.
postmortem_actions: - Add automated alerting for fragmentation ratio and tombstone growth beyond thresholds.
- Expand nightly KV compaction to run across more shards in hosted by default.
- Document best-practices for customers: recommended session lifetime and cache TTL guidance.
- Schedule a follow-up in 6 weeks to review telemetry and decide on hybrid cache pilot.
notes_for_support: If a customer reports similar OOMs: 1) ask for heap profile and last 10 cache inserts, 2) recommend temporary concurrency cap, 3) schedule node restart during maintenance window, 4) escalate to runtime-oncall with attachment.
